messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert 3412345678 created by monitoring - p99 latency > 2.5s for streaming endpoints in eu-west-1
maya (oncall): seeing same in console, p95 ~ 800ms, p99 ~ 3.1s for stream-read route. error budget burn starting.
maya (oncall): quick check - is this an infra flake or cache-related?
lina-eng: I see a spike in cache miss rate for prefix cache on the serving lane. Miss rate jumped from 4% -> 38% around 3412345600.
tony_sre: confirmed. Paging rates to NVMe spike too. Looks correlated: when prefix cache misses go up, we fall back to cold KV which paginates and stalls tail tokens.
maya (oncall): any recent rollouts touching prefix hashing or cache invalidation?
lina-eng: Rollout: prefix-hash v7 deployed to ~30% traffic at 3412345200. Also applied a small TTL tweak (kv-prefix-ttl -> 180s -> 60s) in eu-west-1.
ops-christine: that TTL change was to reduce stale keys, but maybe too aggressive.
maya (oncall): can we confirm per-shard hit rates?
lina-eng: logs: ```
# sample per-shard metric (minute window)
shard-3: hit=61% miss=39% latency_kv=18ms
shard-7: hit=59% miss=41% latency_kv=20ms
shard-2: hit=87% miss=13% latency_kv=6ms
```
maya (oncall): p99 traces show streaming stalls waiting on kv-get for ~120-300ms repeatedly, leading to backpressure and p99 token latency 2-3s.
tony_sre: mitigation plan: 1) rollback prefix-hash v7 rollout to 0% in eu-west-1 2) increase kv-prefix-ttl back to 180s 3) enable streaming-fallback to mux to dedicated cache layer for warm keys 4) rate-limit cold-path to prevent paging surge.
maya (oncall): start rollback now? who can execute?
lina-eng: I can cut the rollout. Running:
```
# controller rollback
rictl rollout set prefix-hash:v6 --region eu-west-1 --traffic 100%
```
lina-eng: done - controller reports traffic now pinned to v6 (~3412345752).
incident-bot: Deploy event: prefix-hash rollout updated by lina-eng at 3412345752.
maya (oncall): ops-christine please bump TTL back.
ops-christine: applying TTL change: `kvctl set-prefix-ttl --region eu-west-1 --ttl 180s`
ops-christine: applied at 3412345770.
tony_sre: enabling streaming fallback and cold-path rate limit now. Commands below.
```
# enable fallback
rictl config set streaming.fallback.enabled true --region eu-west-1
# set cold-path qps cap
rictl config set kv.coldpath.qps 1500 --region eu-west-1
```
tony_sre: fallback enabled and qps cap applied (3412345784).
maya (oncall): metrics update?
lina-eng: within ~30s of rollback+ttl change: prefix cache miss dropped from 38% -> 8% and p99 decreased from 3.1s -> 710ms. NVMe paging rates down 6x.
incident-bot: Severity downgraded to SEV3.
customer-success-jake: FYI, observability shows ~12 customer API keys experienced >1 request with elevated latency (p99) between 3412345600-3412345780. No error spikes, just slow responses. We should notify impacted customers.
maya (oncall): agree. I'll open a short customer-notif draft and tag CS.
maya (oncall): drafting: "We experienced elevated streaming latencies in eu-west-1 due to a prefix cache rollout + TTL change that increased cache misses and triggered paging. Mitigation rolled back and TTL reverted; p99s are back to normal. We're running a full postmortem."
customer-success-jake: thanks - I'll review and send to the small set of impacted accounts.
tony_sre: next steps for follow-up: - postmortem owner (lina-eng) - collect canary logs to compare v6 vs v7 prefix mapping - run a synthetic workload to validate TTL and rollout safety - add automated guard that blocks TTL < 90s during rollouts
lina-eng: taking postmortem. Will paste analysis + key graphs in doc.
maya (oncall): handoff: I'm oncall until 08:00 UTC, but tony_sre will take over incident tracking and coordinate postmortem. If anything regresses, page me immediately.
tony_sre: ack - I've created incident tracker and invited SRE + Eng. Also will add a rollback-validation test to the preflight.
maya (oncall): marking incident resolved for live mitigations. :white_check_mark: Please add timeline entries to the incident doc.
incident-bot: Incident 3412345678 marked mitigated at 3412345889 by maya (oncall).
maya (oncall): closing thread, moving to postmortem channel after we collect graphs. Good triage.
